items.quote: Uploading my old CV and getting a cleaned-up, ATS-ready version back in minutes saved me a whole weekend.
I like that it pulls jobs straight from company career pages, not just the same recycled listings I'd already seen everywhere else.
Having Arabic and English both feel native, not like an afterthought, made this the first job tool that actually felt built for us.
The application tracker is what finally got me organized — I could actually see which companies I still owed a follow-up.
One-click apply on the boards that support it is a genuine time saver when you're applying to a dozen roles a week.
The AI assistant answering my interview-prep questions felt like having a career coach on call at 11pm.

reverse-chronological.label: Reverse-Chronological
reverse-chronological.description: The standard, most widely expected format — skills, then your work history, most recent first.

functional.label: Functional / Skills-Based
functional.description: Leads with skills and any custom sections (e.g. key projects) — good for career changes or employment gaps.

combination.label: Combination / Hybrid
combination.description: Full work history up front, blended with a strong skills section — the modern all-purpose default.

ats-friendly.label: ATS-Friendly
ats-friendly.description: Plain, single-column layout with no colors or graphics — built to parse cleanly through automated screening.

academic-cv.label: Academic CV
academic-cv.description: Education leads, with room for publications, research, and teaching experience right after it.

executive.label: Executive
executive.description: Key achievements get top billing right after your summary — built for senior/leadership roles.
